trust_decision.summary: Deno.upgradeWebSocket decides whether a request is a valid WebSocket upgrade by splitting the untrusted Upgrade and Connection request header values with the backtracking regex /\s*,\s*/; the fix replaces it with a plain ',' split plus trim.

landing_point.why: The advisory names Deno.upgradeWebSocket, and its single implementation is upgradeWebSocket() in ext/http/01_http.js, exported at ext/http/01_http.js:471 and exposed at runtime/js/90_deno_ns.js:139.

fix_sites.entry_point: Deno.upgradeWebSocket(request) public API (Upgrade header), used from Deno.serveHttp and Deno.serve (flash) handlers
fix_sites.module_kind: runtime JS extension (ext/http), the public API implementation

fix_sites.entry_point: Deno.upgradeWebSocket(request) public API (Connection header), same function
fix_sites.module_kind: runtime JS extension (ext/http), the public API implementation

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The flash server (ext/flash/01_http.js:27, :309) reuses the same ext/http upgradeWebSocket through the shared _ws symbol. It has no separate header-splitting copy.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route into this sink. The two fixed lines sit next to each other in one function and are obvious together.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Multi-token Upgrade and Connection headers with optional whitespace, e.g. 'keep-alive, Upgrade' or 'Upgrade,keep-alive', and case-insensitive matching must still be accepted. Over-strict exact-match checks would break them (there is a dedicated test: cli/tests/testdata/run/websocket_server_multi_field_connection_header_test.ts).

O6_input_shapes: Upgrade header with comma-separated tokens and surrounding whitespace
Connection header with comma-separated tokens and surrounding whitespace

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The Sec-WebSocket-Protocol value is split with the literal ', '. A maintainer could plausibly have used the same /\s*,\s*/ regex here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same function and the same comma-list header idiom, a few lines below the fixed sites. It is still a where-type copy that a single search finds.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A flash-specific upgrade helper that checks the Upgrade/Connection tokens itself with a whitespace-tolerant regex
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Flash already has its own upgradeHttpRaw. A second implementation of the header check in another package would be plausible, but it would be planted, not real.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333): a super-linear regex split on untrusted HTTP request header values

O10_build.toolchain: cargo / rustc (V8 via rusty_v8 prebuilt download during build)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Split on ',' and trim each token in both header checks, which is exactly the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: Other regexes run on untrusted request headers, for a different sink (Request/Response Content-Type parsing): ext/fetch/20_headers.js:186-187 uses the global [\t ]+$ suffix regex (ext/web/00_infra.js:86-89) via getDecodeSplitHeader (ext/fetch/23_request.js:285). Possibly quadratic on long interior space runs; not pursued.
httpTrim at ext/web/00_infra.js:272-276 uses ^[ws]*(.*?)[ws]*$ (ext/web/00_infra.js:91-93) on header values and could backtrack. It is a separate sink and was not pursued.
ext/web/01_mimesniff.js:44-45 and :81 use the same suffix-regex idiom when parsing MIME types.
unverified: O1 is counted as 1 public API. The two server front ends (Deno.serveHttp in ext/http, Deno.serve in ext/flash) both reach it through the shared function, and I did not count them separately.
I did not measure whether the out-of-scope regexes in ext/web/00_infra.js are actually super-linear in V8, or whether hyper's header size limits bound them.
The fix diff adds no tests, so regression_tests_in_pinned_commit does not apply. Hidden tests would have to be written from scratch.
